 Cummins Recalls 2,960 Onan Dual-Fuel Generators Over Fuel-Spray Hazard
 Published Nov 15, 2026 9:48 PM EST 
 By
 Joseph James 
 Joe Raedle | Getty Images 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on WhatsApp 
 Cummins is recalling about 2,960 Onan P5000iDF EFI dual-fuel portable generators because pressure can build inside the gasoline tank and force fuel out or eject the fuel cap, the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission announced Nov. 12. The hazard can cause serious injury from fire and burns .
 The company has received 11 reports of fuel discharging and fuel caps ejecting unexpectedly. In one case, a consumer was splashed in the face with fuel but did not need medical attention.
 Many households keep a portable generator ready for winter storms, hurricane season, or RV trips. Owners of this model should stop using it now and check whether their unit is included, rather than wait for the next power outage to find out.
 The Recalled Generator and the Hazard
 The recall covers Cummins Onan P5000iDF EFI Dual Fuel Portable Generators sold in dark gray. They can run on gasoline or propane and produce 4,500 to 5,000 watts, depending on fuel.
 "Cummins" is printed in white on the front and on the handle above the control panel. The Cummins "C" logo and "Onan P5000iDF EFI" are printed on the side.
 The generators were sold at Camping World, Factory Pure, Northern Tool, and AP Electric stores, and online at Cummins.com, from May 2025 through August 2026 for $1,640 to $1,930, according to ConsumerAffairs .
 The problem is a manufacturing error. Valves were installed incorrectly, which keeps fuel vapors from venting properly from the gasoline tank. As pressure builds, fuel can spray out or the cap can pop off. The CPSC recall number is 27-087.
 Portable generators see the heaviest use during winter storms and hurricanes, when owners often refuel in the dark or in a hurry. Those are the moments when a pressurized tank is most dangerous, because gasoline sprayed near a hot engine can ignite. The recall covers units sold over about 15 months, so people who received one as a gift or bought it secondhand should check too.
 Checking the Model and Part Number
 Not every P5000iDF is affected, so the part number matters. A label on the side of the generator lists both the model and part number, according to the CPSC notice.
 Owners can enter that information on Cummins' recall lookup page to see whether their unit is included. Cummins can be reached at 800-286-6467, Monday through Friday.
 If the unit is included, the remedy is a free repair at an authorized Cummins service location, which owners can find through the company's service locator . Owners should not try to fix the valves themselves.
 Taking a photo of the side label before calling makes the process faster. It also helps to keep the purchase receipt, though the recall notice does not say one is required. Owners can ask the service center about turnaround time and whether a repair appointment can be scheduled in advance.
 An unrepaired unit should not be sold, traded, or given away. Federal law prohibits selling products under a voluntary recall conducted with the CPSC, and owners who have trouble getting the remedy can report the problem to the agency through its website.
 Safe Handling Before the Repair
 Gasoline spray is the immediate danger. Anyone who has a recalled generator with fuel in the tank should keep it outdoors, away from flames, pilot lights, and other ignition sources, and let it cool fully before touching the fuel cap. Owners with questions about emptying the tank can ask Cummins or the service center for instructions.
 If fuel gets on the skin or in the eyes, rinse with plenty of water and remove soaked clothing. Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 offers free guidance. Burns, eye pain that does not ease, or trouble breathing after inhaling fumes need medical care.
 RV owners and campers should avoid storing a fueled generator inside an enclosed truck bed cover, trailer compartment, or vehicle, where vapor and pressure could build unnoticed. A ventilated outdoor spot is safer until the repair is done.
 Families who depend on electricity for medical needs face the biggest bind. Home oxygen concentrators, CPAP machines, insulin storage, and powered wheelchairs all need backup power. Those households can ask their utility about medical priority lists, check whether a neighbor or local shelter has power, and arrange a loaner or rental while the generator is repaired.
 Year-Round Generator Safety Still Applies
 The recall involves fuel, but carbon monoxide remains the leading generator danger. The CPSC warns that portable generators should be run only outdoors , far from windows, doors, and vents, and never in a home, garage, or crawl space, even with doors open. Working CO alarms on every level of the home add another layer of protection.
 Refueling also deserves care with any model. Turning the generator off and letting it cool before adding gasoline lowers the risk of fire. Storing fuel in approved containers away from living spaces helps too.
 Generator recalls tied to fuel leaks are not new. Westinghouse recalled about 7,500 dual-fuel generators in 2020 because fuel could leak from the fuel filter, Consumer Reports noted . Owners of any generator can check CPSC.gov periodically, especially before storm season.
 Cummins has not said how long repairs will take. MedicalDaily will report if the recall expands or if injuries are reported.

 Key Questions Answered
 Which generator is recalled? The Cummins Onan P5000iDF EFI Dual Fuel Portable Generator, sold in dark gray.
 How many units are affected? About 2,960.
 What is the hazard? Incorrectly installed valves can let pressure build in the gas tank, causing fuel to spray out or the cap to eject.
 Has anyone been hurt? Cummins received 11 reports, including one consumer who was splashed in the face with fuel and did not need medical attention.
 How do I check my unit? Find the model and part number on the label on the side and enter it on Cummins' recall page, or call 800-286-6467.
 What is the remedy? A free repair at an authorized Cummins service location.
 Where was it sold? Camping World, Factory Pure, Northern Tool, and AP Electric stores, and Cummins.com, from May 2025 through August 2026.
